title: Bound transcript page bytes and live body updates without breaking offsets or history navigation
outcome: Use existing transcript/history and body-sequence owners to serve bounded encoded pages and on-demand large message bodies; bound client retention and repair queues.
acceptance: Tail/history and live message, textReplace, commandUpdate and nested message payloads have enforced encoded-byte budgets before full body materialization; one oversized message remains retrievable through a stable bounded body-range mechanism.

Partial bodies carry explicit completeness, total-length and revision/offset metadata; no silently truncated text or successful full-body claim; existing body-sequence and resync invariants remain valid.
Clients stop applying full-body offsets to partial bodies, bound retained repair deltas and non-visible transcript residency by bytes, and preserve older/newer navigation and copy semantics.

Focused boundary and recovery tests cover escaping, a single oversized body, short pages, concurrent updates and client resync without large allocations; standard independent review and full gate pass.
